title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The step b(s'(d)) = b(b'(d)) is not among the relations (38) as stated on p. 58. It holds only because Σ*(2) is taken as a (closed) subspace of the fibre product Σ*(1) ×_{b,Σ,b} Σ*(1) with s', b' the two projections, as made explicit in the Scholie on p. 60. This should be listed as an axiom.
Notational drift: Σ_*(1), Σ(1), Σ_1 and Σ*(1) are used interchangeably for the same space, as are Σ(2) and Σ*(2).
Antisymmetry is not stated separately, but it follows from transitivity plus irreflexivity, so the conclusion 'strict order' is correct.

The conclusion that ≺ is an order 'on Σ' (on points) sits slightly awkwardly with the Scholie on p. 60, which speaks of a total order on the codimension-1 strata through each boundary point. These are two different (though related) order structures, and the passage between them is not spelled out.

ideas.what: Deriving a strict partial order from boundary-immersion/collapse data by a cartesian-square (fibre product) condition: transitivity via the unique lift d, then w = s'(d).
ideas.modern_name: Segal condition for a 2-truncated semi-simplicial space; thin non-unital internal category (topological poset) whose nerve is (Σ, Σ*(1), Σ*(2))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1968/1974) for the Segal condition; internal categories go back to Ehresmann
ideas.where_published: Internal categories and nerves appear in Grothendieck's descent/FGA-era work and in Pursuing Stacks, but not this specific stratified-space use

ideas.what: Encoding a stratified space by its unfolding: a space with a proper boundary immersion b of codim-1 strata and collapse maps s, with compatible corner data in codimension 2 (cartesian squares).
ideas.modern_name: Resolution of Thom–Mather stratified spaces into manifolds with fibred corners / iterated fibration structures; 'unzipping' of conically smooth stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Melrose and coauthors; Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017); earlier Verona and Thom–Mather-style blow-ups
ideas.where_published: Only alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (§5-6, 'déploiement' of stratified spaces / tame topology); details unpublished

ideas.what: Recovering Σ*(1) as the graph of the strict order and Σ*(2) as the space of length-2 flags, with the structure maps as nerve face maps.
ideas.modern_name: Nerve of a (topological) poset; exit-path / stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; exit-path categories via MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (HA Appendix A)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axioms for the déploiement are formulated as a low-degree simplicial object satisfying a Segal-type cartesian condition: boundary immersion b, collapse s, codim-2 corner space Σ*(2) with the square b∘p2 = s∘b' cartesian. The induced structure is the nerve of a topological strict order. This anticipates presenting the resolution of a stratified space as an internal category/semi-simplicial space in spaces, linking the analytic 'manifolds with fibred corners' picture (Melrose, ALMP) and the homotopical 'stratified spaces as functors to posets / exit-path ∞-categories' picture (Lurie, AFT). The literature mostly develops these two pictures separately.
missed.quote: donc la relation x ≺ y est la relation d'inégalité stricte associée à une relation d'ordre sur Σ. On récupère, Σ(1) comme le graphe de la relation d'ordre stricte, Σ(2) comme les drapeaux x ≺ y ≺ z de longueur 2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a compact, purely categorical axiomatisation of iterated boundary-fibration (corner) structures: it is a Segal condition. It could be compared with AFT's unzipping and with blow-up / corner-structure axioms in Melrose's b-calculus. The argument on this page itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The proof is a routine verification that a Segal-type fibre-product condition gives transitivity. The mild interest is that Grothendieck's déploiement axioms are framed as a nerve/internal-category structure, which is a modern-looking formulation of corner/fibration structures. That is suggestive but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Σ_*(1)' should read Σ*(1) (same space as on p. 58).
'∃! d ∈ Σ(2)' and 'w = s'(d) ∈ Σ(1)': the manuscript means Σ*(2) and Σ*(1).
In the irreflexivity line the source of (p1; b) is the codim-1 space Σ*(1), written loosely as Σ_1 in the manuscript.
'On récupère, Σ(1)' is more plausibly 'On récupère enfin Σ(1)' (the manuscript seems to read 'On récupère, enfin,' or similar).
In the image, the struck-out symbol before 'u = p1 v' is an overwritten b (a correction), not a separate term.
